name: LP5907MFX-3.3_NOPB
title: 250 mA low-noise, low-IQ LDO regulator, fixed outputs 1.2 V to 4.5 V
summary: The LP5907 is a fixed-output linear regulator for up to 250 mA, running from 2.2 V to 5.5 V and aimed at noise-sensitive RF and analog loads: 6.5 µVRMS output noise, 82 dB rejection at 1 kHz, 12 µA quiescent current. It is stable with 1 µF ceramic capacitors at input and output and needs no noise-filter capacitor; the output capacitor may sit up to 10 cm away. Outputs from 1.2 V to 4.5 V come in 25 mV steps, in SOT-23-5, 1 mm X2SON-4 and four 4-ball DSBGA packages. LP5907MFX-3.3/NOPB is the 3.3 V part in SOT-23 (DBV), on reels of 3000, marked LLVB.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The whole regulator: the supply comes in on IN with a 1 µF capacitor to ground, the 1 µF output capacitor sits on OUT, and EN is brought out as its own control input. Either capacitor may be made larger than 1 µF.
notes: The design example built on this circuit is a 1.8 V output at 200 mA from 2.2 V to 5.5 V.

where.PD-MAX: highest dissipation the package can carry

equations.name: Maximum ambient temperature
equations.note: If TA-MAX cannot come down, PD has to, by lowering VIN (keeping it at or above its minimum), lowering IOUT, or both.

operation.text: A band-gap reference of 1.20 V feeds an error amplifier through an RC filter, driving a pass device from IN to OUT. Noise on the reference is removed by a single-pole RC filter whose –3 dB corner is near 0.1 Hz. No external noise capacitor is needed.

EN is pulled to GND inside by 1 MΩ, so an open EN leaves the regulator off. EN must be above VIH (1.2 V) for the part to be on in every condition and below VIL (0.4 V) for it to be fully off with the output discharge working. Off, the part draws typically under 1 µA. The driving source must swing beyond both thresholds; where shutdown is not used, EN may be tied straight to IN.
With EN low and the regulator off, a 230 Ω (typ) resistor inside pulls OUT to ground, emptying COUT.

The output switches off when the junction reaches about 160 °C and comes back once it has cooled to about 145 °C; with enough dissipation the part cycles. It covers brief overloads only: it does not stand in for heat sinking, and running into it continuously can shorten the part's life.

There is no dedicated undervoltage lockout. The internal circuits are not fully working below VIN = 2.2 V, and the output is regulated only once VIN reaches the larger of 2.2 V and VOUT + VDO. For full regulation and dynamic performance the supply should be at least VOUT + 1 V, clean and tightly regulated.
The regulator is stable and stays in regulation with no load at all.

At least 1 µF from IN to a clean analog ground, no more than 1 cm from the IN pin, is needed for stability across the full load range; ceramic, tantalum or film all work. For good load-transient response CIN should be at least as large as COUT. With long leads from the battery or source, or where ground impedance and input inductance cannot be kept low, use 10 µF or more. A tantalum input part needs a surge-current rating suited to a low-impedance source. After tolerance, DC bias and temperature, the effective capacitance must never fall under 0.7 µF.

A ceramic X5R or X7R part of 1 µF to 10 µF with ESR between 5 mΩ and 500 mΩ is suitable, connected from OUT with a good return to GND. Tantalum or film also work but cost more and take more room. A typical 1 µF ceramic has 20 mΩ to 40 mΩ ESR. X7R holds its value within ±15 % over temperature. Tantalum ESR roughly doubles from 25 °C to –40 °C, so margin is needed. The effective value must stay above 0.7 µF over all conditions.

OUT needs at least 1 µF, but that capacitance can be up to 10 cm away, so a capacitor already at the load's input can serve. Keep the trace inductance from OUT to the capacitors under 35 nH: wide traces, the output layer close to ground, no vias or else many in parallel. Where load steps are fast, make the input capacitance at least equal to the total on the output node.

PSRR, noise and transient response depend on the board. Mount CIN and COUT on the regulator's face of the board, as near to it as practical, and return both grounds to the GND pin with short, wide copper. Long or narrow traces and vias add inductance and resistance that hurt transient behaviour.
The thermal pad of the X2SON package is soldered to the board for heat flow and mechanical strength.

The DSBGA package has its own assembly method; alignment marks on the board help placement. Direct light on a DSBGA part, most of all red and infrared such as from halogen lamps nearby, can upset operation; ordinary fluorescent room light has little effect.
Fixed output voltages are made from 1.2 V to 4.5 V in 25 mV steps.
An automotive-qualified version is the LP5907-Q1.
